affectedPublicSurfaces: NO NEW PUBLIC SURFACE — no route, no request or response model, no schema change. What DOES change is what a seller sees happen: a suspended run that the seller has touched by hand now ENDS instead of proceeding, with `seller_modified` (#1707's cause) on the run row and therefore on `GET /demo/runs` and the SSE stream. S-FR-8's promise — 'Juli never overrides my hand' — becomes enforceable code rather than a stated intention.

THE RESUME PATH IN `services/agent/runner/core.py`. A run that is suspended snapshots WHAT IT CREATED at the moment of the write (activity fields; stock level per warehouse), and on ANY resume signal re-reads the real thing and compares. The re-read is a fresh vendor READ, which makes this the same shape as S-FR-5's re-verify-before-the-write — and the two must not be conflated: re-verify guards a write that is about to happen, the intervention guard decides whether the run continues at all.

THE DIVERGENCE VERDICT IS ASYMMETRIC AND MUST BE. Divergence NOT ORIGINATED BY JULI ends the run; a difference Juli itself wrote does not. That distinction is what makes the guard usable, and it is the one place a naive equality check gets it wrong — a run that just wrote a discount would find the activity 'changed' and end itself immediately. Compare against the snapshot Juli took AFTER its own write, and say in the PR how a Juli-originated change is told apart from a seller's.

IT WRITES NOTHING WHEN IT ENDS. No deactivate call, no stock write, no vendor mutation of any kind on the divergence path — asserted on a recording transport, because 'Juli reverts nothing' (S-FR-8) is the whole point and a compensating write would be the exact opposite of the promise.

IT RECORDS A COMPLETION ACT — which means it depends on #1713's WRITER, not just on #1712's table. The issue lists only #1707 and #1708 as blockers; the act-record writer lands in #1713 (itself blocked by #1712 and #1707). Sequence #1715 after #1713 or its first acceptance criterion cannot be satisfied.

IT MARKS THE SUBJECT SO NO CARD RE-ISSUES, and it does so through #1703's EXISTING vocabulary: the card is suppressed with `basis_unchanged` until the subject's basis snapshot changes. That is a reuse of the revision-suppression concept, deliberately NOT the emission budget's `active_cap`/`cooldown`/`weekly_novelty_cap`.

SHARED BY CLEAR EXCESS AND REPLENISH. This lands ONCE, in the shared runner, and never as a private copy inside a workflow lane — forking it is how two workflows end up disagreeing about what counts as intervention.

The whole path is driven through the REAL `WorkflowRunner` resume with the vendor bound to a RECORDING FAKE built on the real client's signature, so 'no deactivate call was made' is observed at the wire; the signal arrives through #1708's REAL webhook consumer, never by calling the guard directly. migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE IN THIS SLICE. The creation snapshot lives in the run's existing `state` JSON on `workflow_runs`; the terminal cause `seller_modified` is already in the enum and in the widened `ck_workflow_runs_stop_reason` CHECK from #1707; the suspended state and its timer are #1706's; the completion act record is written into #1712's table through #1713's writer; and the card suppression reuses #1703's `basis_unchanged`. Do not open a migration file — if any of those is missing, a dependency is unmet and the answer is to report it, not to add a column. Old and new code coexist because the deployed schema is identical before and after; only the resume path's decision changes.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. A suspended run has no intervention guard, so a seller who edits the activity or the stock line Juli created would find Juli proceeding over the top of them once a resume path exists. Nothing about the deployed system changes today — `optimize_product_2` never suspends externally and no second workflow ships until W9-B — so this is a promise not yet made rather than a promise broken. Nothing is exposed, nothing is partially applied.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Code-only rollback: redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker. There is NO schema to revert and NO downgrade to run — this slice owns no migration. Runs already ended `seller_modified` stay ended and their completion act records stay readable; the previous code does not enumerate the cause but `RunListItem.stop_reason` is a plain `str | None` on the way out, so nothing breaks on read. THE HAZARD TO STATE IN THE PR: a run still SUSPENDED across the rollback loses its guard, so the next signal will resume it WITHOUT comparing against the creation snapshot — meaning Juli could write over a seller's hand, the precise thing S-FR-8 forbids. Drain, reap or let expire the externally-waiting runs BEFORE rolling back, or accept that risk explicitly; do not let it be discovered. If #1701's, #1706's, #1707's, #1709's or #1712's schema is being reverted in the same operation, those downgrades are theirs and must FAIL LOUDLY on any non-product `subject_type` row, NULL `product_id`, `waiting_external` row, new stop-reason cause, non-default confirmation `kind`, or any act-record row. Order: previous code first, any schema revert second.

doNotInfer: Do NOT read a migration number from head — do NOT write a migration at all. Every column, state, cause and table this slice uses belongs to #1701, #1703, #1706, #1707 and #1712. The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. The chain's single head today is `055_juli_app_sync_state_update` (revising `054_juli_app_bronze_select`), but W6 and W8 both hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries two same-numbered `043_*` files (`043_stop_reason_consent_pause` and `043_juli_app_role`, chained one after the other) from exactly this mistake.

Do NOT write anything on the divergence path. No deactivate, no stock write, no compensating or reverting write — S-FR-8 says Juli reverts nothing. Assert zero requests on a recording transport, not a branch not taken.

Do NOT treat Juli's OWN write as intervention. The snapshot is taken AFTER Juli's write; a naive equality check against the pre-write state would end every run the instant its own webhook came back. State in the PR how a Juli-originated change is distinguished.
Do NOT compare a summed stock total. Compare per warehouse — a rebalance that leaves the total unchanged is still a seller's hand on the stock line.
Do NOT treat an unreadable vendor state as 'unchanged'. A failed re-read fails closed with an existing named error and an honest terminal status; a world you cannot see is not permission to act.
Do NOT invent a new stop reason. `seller_modified` is #1707's and the vocabulary is closed; a cause coined here would fail the CHECK constraint anyway.

Do NOT reuse the emission-budget suppression vocabulary. Marking an intervened subject uses #1703's `basis_unchanged`, not `active_cap`, `cooldown` or `weekly_novelty_cap` (`services/action_cards/emission_budget.py`) — those are the budget's reasons for not surfacing a card and mean something else entirely.
Do NOT block the subject forever. Suppression lasts UNTIL the basis snapshot changes; a permanent block would silently retire a subject the seller never asked Juli to stop managing.

Do NOT fork a private copy of this guard into a workflow lane. It lands ONCE in the shared runner; Clear Excess and Replenish both consume it, and two copies would let them disagree about what intervention means.

Do NOT add a push, email or Zalo transport to tell the seller the run ended. The completion act record (#1712's table via #1713's writer) is the entire notification in v1; `services/alerts/` has no callers and `FcmAdapter._deliver` is a `fcm_send_stub`.

Do NOT gate a stage on a checklist tick, do NOT derive the subject from revenue, do NOT emit a per-order card, and do NOT add a second reaper policy object — a signal that never arrives already degrades to #1706's `external_wait_timeout_h`.
